newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shr rally continues with 7th record close.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shr rally continues with 7th record close.

text.p: The Caracas Stock Exchange general index surged to a seventh consecutive record high in heavy trade as rate increases for market leader Electricidad de Caracas boosted an already bullish market, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share IBC index rose 2.74 percent to 8,801.23.

Electricidad followed a 43.00 bolivar rise Thursday with another 33.00 bolivar increase to close at 725.00 bolivars as the magnitude of a recently approved tariff increase trickled through to the market.
Rafael Ponte, Electricidad's head of rates and markets, told Reuters Friday the rate hike was equivalent to about 75 percent over six months -- well above market expectations.
"This boosted the market considerably," said Bancaracas broker William Boulton.
A total of 33 stocks rose, 10 fell and four closed flat in trade of 22.266 billion bolivars ($45.8 million).
"There was high demand in the market, especially from foreign investors," Boulton said.
Foreigners have been drawn by a recent series of reforms and initiatives including the opening up of the state oil industry and removal of outdated labor laws, brokers said.

Among other leading stocks, telephone company CANTV rose 10.00 bolivars to 2,990.00 bolivars, while cement company Vencemos class 1 stock rose 20.00 bolivars to 640.00 bolivars and class 2 stock rose 64.00 bolivars to 564.00 bolivars.
Bullish sentiment on Venezuela's economic prospects and the increase in electric rates saw the index rise 9.9 percent for the week.
Brokers said that although profit-taking was always likely, the market appeared to be set for further rises next week.
